reading.body:
A single unconfirmed address in Tempe, Arizona does not describe an active data center, and it carries zero published power capacity.

The entry rests on an OpenStreetMap node tagged as a data center. Reverse geocoding of its coordinates returns only a building at 2005 West 14th Street, Tempe, with no business name attached. No operator website, business registration, or press coverage naming J-Curve Technologies at that location could be confirmed, and research status is recorded as exhausted. The name itself is more common in finance than in technology.

This matters for AI because the grid constraint is measured in megawatts, and this row contributes none. Arizona has 56 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 publish power specifications totaling 512 MW. A facility with no confirmed operator and no published specifications cannot be ranked among them, so it does not enter any accounting of AI scaling constraints or grid load in the state.

What the data does not tell the reader is whether any computing happens at this address. It records an unresolved mapping entry, not a finding that the site is empty or inactive. The honest reading is that the facility is unknown, and unknown capacity is not the same as zero capacity.
